```{r} 
library(tidyverse)
```

## patient data###
```{r}
patientidentifier <- read_excel("E:/Daten(x)/Daten(lw-r)/Abc/Doktorarbeit SJS/Analyse R-Statistics/gender plots/gender_info_full.xlsx",
           sheet = 1, skip = 1 ) %>% 
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo") %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = 3:4,
               names_to = "gender",
               values_to = "numberofpatient") %>% 
  filter(numberofpatient== 1)
patientidentifier
```


### GPT ####################################################################################

```{r}

# gptaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# gptaltdata$`GPT Day11` <- as.numeric(gptaltdata$`GPT Day11`)

# gptaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- gpt_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts back with the original data
gptaltdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- gptaltdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)

  
```

## alt data greater than 5 counts in all attribute###
```{r}
gpt_gender_full <- left_join(patientidentifier, gpt_full, by = "Edited_BfArM Nummer2") %>%
  select(1,2,3,6,7) %>%
  drop_na(labreads) %>%
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|_DBS")) 
gpt_gender_full
```


```{r}
gpt_gender_full %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% normality(labreads)
```



```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- gpt_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = gpt_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_gpt_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "GPT U/L",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
gpt_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(gpt_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/gpt_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(gpt_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
 ##### Make the line plot of labreads for male and female####

###############################################################################
gpt_summary_data <- gpt_min3  %>% filter(gender == "Female") %>% ## change (male and female for data to make grgpth)
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_labread = mean(labreads, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_labread = sd(labreads, na.rm = TRUE),
    sem_labread = sd(labreads, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    count = n() 
    )

gpt_summary_data$attribute <- 
   factor(gpt_summary_data$attribute,levels = c("GPT Day1", "GPT Day2", "GPT Day3","GPT Day4","GPT Day5", "GPT Day6","GPT Day7","GPT Day8","GPT Day9","GPT Day10", "GPT Day11","GPT Day12","GPT Day13","GPT Day14","GPT Day15","GPT Day16","GPT Day17","GPT Day18","GPT Day19","GPT Day20","GPT Day21","GPT Day22","GPT Day23","GPT Day24","GPT Day25","GPT Day26","GPT Day27","GPT Day28","GPT Day29","GPT Day30","GPT Day31","GPT Day32","GPT Day33","GPT Day34","GPT Day35","GPT Day36","GPT Day37","GPT Day38","GPT Day39","GPT Day40","GPT Day41","GPT Day42","GPT Day43","GPT Day44","GPT Day45","GPT Day46","GPT Day47","GPT Day48","GPT Day49","GPT Day50","GPT Day51","GPT Day52","GPT Day53","GPT Day54","GPT Day55","GPT Day56","GPT Day57","GPT Day58","GPT Day59","GPT Day60","GPT Day61","GPT Day62","GPT Day63","GPT Day64","GPT Day65","GPT Day66","GPT Day67","GPT Day68","GPT Day69","GPT Day70","GPT Day71","GPT Day72","GPT Day73","GPT Day74","GPT Day75","GPT Day76","GPT Day77","GPT Day78","GPT Day79","GPT Day80","GPT Day81","GPT Day82","GPT Day83","GPT Day84","GPT Day85","GPT Day86","GPT Day87","GPT Day88","GPT Day89","GPT Day90","GPT Day91","GPT Day92","GPT Day93","GPT Day94","GPT Day95","GPT Day96","GPT Day97","GPT Day98","GPT Day99","GPT Day100"))

### for lineplot
gpt_min3$attribute <- factor(gpt_min3$attribute,levels = c("GPT Day1", "GPT Day2", "GPT Day3","GPT Day4","GPT Day5", "GPT Day6","GPT Day7","GPT Day8","GPT Day9","GPT Day10", "GPT Day11","GPT Day12","GPT Day13","GPT Day14","GPT Day15","GPT Day16","GPT Day17","GPT Day18","GPT Day19","GPT Day20","GPT Day21","GPT Day22","GPT Day23","GPT Day24","GPT Day25","GPT Day26","GPT Day27","GPT Day28","GPT Day29","GPT Day30","GPT Day31","GPT Day32","GPT Day33","GPT Day34","GPT Day35","GPT Day36","GPT Day37","GPT Day38","GPT Day39","GPT Day40","GPT Day41","GPT Day42","GPT Day43","GPT Day44","GPT Day45","GPT Day46","GPT Day47","GPT Day48","GPT Day49","GPT Day50","GPT Day51","GPT Day52","GPT Day53","GPT Day54","GPT Day55","GPT Day56","GPT Day57","GPT Day58","GPT Day59","GPT Day60","GPT Day61","GPT Day62","GPT Day63","GPT Day64","GPT Day65","GPT Day66","GPT Day67","GPT Day68","GPT Day69","GPT Day70","GPT Day71","GPT Day72","GPT Day73","GPT Day74","GPT Day75","GPT Day76","GPT Day77","GPT Day78","GPT Day79","GPT Day80","GPT Day81","GPT Day82","GPT Day83","GPT Day84","GPT Day85","GPT Day86","GPT Day87","GPT Day88","GPT Day89","GPT Day90","GPT Day91","GPT Day92","GPT Day93","GPT Day94","GPT Day95","GPT Day96","GPT Day97","GPT Day98","GPT Day99","GPT Day100"))


# Create the line plot with rotated x-axis labels and error bars for both SD and SEM
max_value <- max(gpt_summary_data$mean_labread + gpt_summary_data$sem_labread, na.rm = TRUE)
#breaks_up_to_500 <- seq(0, 500, by = 100)
#additional_breaks <- if (max_value > 600) seq(600, max_value, by = 300) else numeric(0)
#all_breaks <- c(breaks_up_to_500, additional_breaks)

gpt_all_groups_line_plot_for_time_course_for_female_with_patient_count <- ggplot(gpt_summary_data, aes(x = attribute, y = mean_labread, group = 1)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_labread, ymax = mean_labread + sd_labread), 
                width = 0.2, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "lightgrey", size = 1, se = FALSE) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -1.5, size = 5) +  
  labs(title = "gpt_all groups_mean gpt in time course for female with patient count", 
       x = "Day of measurement", y = "gpt U/L", cgpttion = "Red error bars: SD") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10), labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ".") )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/gpt_all groups_line plot for time course for female with patient count.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(gpt_all_groups_line_plot_for_time_course_for_female_with_patient_count)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
  filter(Treatment.x == "Leber_Para")

# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- lpgot_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = lpgot_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "liver para_got_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "got U/L",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
got_liver_para_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(lpgot_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/got_liver para_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(got_liver_para_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}

# ggtaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# ggtaltdata$`ggt Day11` <- as.numeric(ggtaltdata$`ggt Day11`)

# ggtaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- ggt_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts back with the original data
ggtdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- ggtdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
filtered_data <- ldh_long %>%

  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts back with the original data
ldhdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- ldhdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- ldh_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = ldh_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_ldh_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "ldh U/L",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
ldh_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(ldh_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/ldh_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(ldh_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
# apaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# apaltdata$`ap Day11` <- as.numeric(apaltdata$`ap Day11`)

# apaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- ap_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts baap with the original data
apdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- apdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# pttaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2)

# pttaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- ptt_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts baptt with the original data
pttdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- pttdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen

  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = ptt_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_ptt_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "ptt Sec.",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen

  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(ptt_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/ptt_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(ptt_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
filtered_data <- leukozyten_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts baleukozyten with the original data
leukozytendata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- leukozytendata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
                width = 0.2, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "lightgrey", size = 1, se = FALSE) +

  # SEM error bars in red
  labs(title = "leukozyten_all groups_mean leukozyten in time course for female with patient count",    ###NEW###
       x = "Day of measurement",                     ###NEW###
       y = "leukozyten /ul",
       cleukozytention = "Red error bars: SD") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = all_breaks,
                     limits = c(0, max_value))

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/leukozyten_all groups_line plot for time course for female with patient count.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(leukozyten_all_groups_line_plot_for_time_course_for_female_with_patient_count)
dev.off()
```

```{r}

# erythrozytenaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# erythrozytenaltdata$`erythrozyten Day11` <- as.numeric(erythrozytenaltdata$`erythrozyten Day11`)

# erythrozytenaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- erythrozyten_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts baerythrozyten with the original data
erythrozytendata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- erythrozytendata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}

counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bathrombozyten with the original data
thrombozytendata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- thrombozytendata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)

  
```

```{r}
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = all_breaks,
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- hb_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bahb with the original data
hbdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- hbdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```


```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- hb_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = hb_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_hb_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "hb g/dl",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
hb_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(hb_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/hb_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(hb_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bagesamteiweiß with the original data
gesamteiweißdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- gesamteiweißdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}

# total_bilirubinaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# total_bilirubinaltdata$`total_bilirubin Day11` <- as.numeric(total_bilirubinaltdata$`total_bilirubin Day11`)

# total_bilirubinaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- total_bilirubin_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts batotal_bilirubin with the original data
total_bilirubindata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- total_bilirubindata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)

  
```

```{r}
total_bilirubin_gender_full <- left_join(patientidentifier, total_bilirubin_full, by = "Edited_BfArM Nummer2") %>%
  select(1,2,3,6,7) %>%
  drop_na(labreads) %>%
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|_DBS")) 
total_bilirubin_gender_full
```


```{r}
total_bilirubin_gender_full %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% normality(labreads)
```



```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- total_bilirubin_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = total_bilirubin_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_total_bilirubin_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "total_bilirubin mg/dl",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
total_bilirubin_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(total_bilirubin_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/total_bilirubin_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(total_bilirubin_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}

# direct_bilirubinaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# direct_bilirubinaltdata$`direct_bilirubin Day11` <- as.numeric(direct_bilirubinaltdata$`direct_bilirubin Day11`)

# direct_bilirubinaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- direct_bilirubin_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts badirect_bilirubin with the original data
direct_bilirubindata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- direct_bilirubindata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)

  
```

```{r}
direct_bilirubin_gender_full
```

```{r}
direct_bilirubin_gender_full %>%
```

```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- direct_bilirubin_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = direct_bilirubin_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_direct_bilirubin_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "direct_bilirubin mg/dl",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
direct_bilirubin_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(direct_bilirubin_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/direct_bilirubin_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(direct_bilirubin_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}

# kreatininaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# kreatininaltdata$`kreatinin Day11` <- as.numeric(kreatininaltdata$`kreatinin Day11`)

# kreatininaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- kreatinin_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bakreatinin with the original data
kreatinindata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- kreatinindata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}

  group_by(gender) %>% normality(labreads)
```



```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- kreatinin_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = kreatinin_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_kreatinin_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "kreatinin mg/dl",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
kreatinin_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(kreatinin_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/kreatinin_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(kreatinin_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
# harnstoffaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# harnstoffaltdata$`harnstoff Day11` <- as.numeric(harnstoffaltdata$`harnstoff Day11`)

# harnstoffaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- harnstoff_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts baharnstoff with the original data
harnstoffdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- harnstoffdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- harnstoff_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = harnstoff_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_harnstoff_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "harnstoff mg/dl",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
harnstoff_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(harnstoff_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/harnstoff_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(harnstoff_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
filtered_data <- crp_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bacrp with the original data
crpdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- crpdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- crp_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = crp_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_crp_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "crp mg/l",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
crp_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(crp_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/crp_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(crp_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}

# kaliumaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2) 
# kaliumaltdata$`kalium Day11` <- as.numeric(kaliumaltdata$`kalium Day11`)

# kaliumaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- kalium_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bakalium with the original data
kaliumdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- kaliumdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# kalziumaltdata <- read_excel("Data/SJS Arun 27.05.24.xlsx", sheet = 2,skip = 2)

# kalziumaltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- kalzium_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bakalzium with the original data
kalziumdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- kalziumdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
kalzium_gender_full %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% normality(labreads)
```



```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- kalzium_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = kalzium_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_kalzium_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "kalzium mmol/l",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
kalzium_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(kalzium_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/kalzium_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(kalzium_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts baquick with the original data
quickdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- quickdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
```

```{r}
# Schritt 1: Anzahl einzigartiger Patienten pro Diabetes-Gruppe berechnen
n_patients <- quick_gender_full %>%
  distinct(`Edited_BfArM Nummer2`, gender) %>%  # nur einzigartige Patienten
  count(gender, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0("N = ", n))

# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = quick_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "all groups_quick_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "quick %",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
quick_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(quick_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/quick_all groups_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(quick_all_groups_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
# inraltdata is raw data from excle
# Step 1: Pivot the data to long format, preserving the identifier
# Step 2: Filter the data for the specified treatment
filtered_data <- inr_long %>%
#  filter(Treatment == "Leber_Diclo")%>% 
  filter(!str_detect(attribute, "_From Start|_From start|Day_Unknown")) ####NEW####

# Step 3: Count occurrences, preserving the identifier
counts_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(attribute) %>%
  summarize(count = sum(!is.na(labreads)), .groups = 'drop')

# Step 4: Merge the counts bainr with the original data
inrdata_with_counts <- filtered_data %>%
  left_join(counts_data, by = "attribute")


# Step 5: Filter the data where count is equal to or higher than 3
 filtered_data_with_min_counts <- inrdata_with_counts %>%
  filter(count >= 3) %>%      ####NEW####
  drop_na(labreads)

# Print the updated data with counts equal to or higher than 3
print(filtered_data_with_min_counts)
```

```{r}
# Schritt 2: ggbetweenstats-Plot erstellen
plot_without_count <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = liinr_gender_full,
  x = "gender",
  y = "labreads",
  type = "np",  # non-parametrisch
  title = "liver ibu_inr_violin plot for gender",
  xlab = "Gender",
  ylab = "inr",
  messages = FALSE)

# Schritt 3: N-Werte oberhalb der Violinenplots einfügen
inr_liver_ibu_violin_plot_for_gender <- plot_without_count+ 
  geom_text(
    data = n_patients,
    aes(x = gender, 
        y = max(liinr_gender_full$labreads, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,  # Position leicht oberhalb
        label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/inr_liver ibu_violin plot for gender.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(inr_liver_ibu_violin_plot_for_gender)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
inr_all_groups_line_plot_for_time_course_for_female_with_patient_count <- ggplot(inr_summary_data, aes(x = attribute, y = mean_labread, group = 1)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_labread, ymax = mean_labread + sd_labread), 
                width = 0.2, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "lightgrey", size = 1, se = FALSE) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -1.5, size = 5) +  
  labs(title = "inr_all groups_mean inr in time course for female with patient count", 
       x = "Day of measurement", y = "inr", cinrtion = "Red error bars: SD") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10), labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ".") )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
svg("plots/inr_all groups_line plot for time course for female with patient count.svg", height = 6, width = 8)
print(inr_all_groups_line_plot_for_time_course_for_female_with_patient_count)
dev.off()
```
